title: Bible Guide
paragraph: PROPHET WITH WHOM THE LORD SPOKE "MOUTH TO MOUTH" (NUMBERS 12:8) · EXODUS & WILDERNESS

blocks.text: PROPHET WITH WHOM THE LORD SPOKE "MOUTH TO MOUTH" (NUMBERS 12:8) · EXODUS & WILDERNESS
Moses. Sent from the bush to Pharaoh; Scripture says no prophet arose in Israel like him.
Called, as four accounts tell it
“God called unto him out of the midst of the bush, and said, Moses, Moses. And he said, Here am I.”
Exodus says "the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend", and Deuteronomy closes with a prophet "whom the LORD knew face to face". Exodus 33:11 Deuteronomy 34:10

When Aaron and Miriam asked whether the LORD had spoken only by Moses, the LORD answered that he makes himself known to a prophet "in a vision" and speaks to him "in a dream", but with Moses "mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches". Numbers 12:6–8
At the tabernacle the LORD promised to speak with Moses "from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims", and Numbers says Moses heard the voice there. Exodus 25:22 Numbers 7:89

At Sinai the people asked Moses, "Speak thou with us, and we will hear: but let not God speak with us". Moses later said he "stood between the LORD and you at that time, to shew you the word of the LORD". Exodus 20:18–21 Deuteronomy 5:4–5

From the textOur count in the KJV: "the LORD spake unto Moses" stands in 105 verses (Exodus 20, Leviticus 33, Numbers 51, Deuteronomy 1) and "the LORD said unto Moses" in 55 (Exodus 36, Leviticus 2, Numbers 13, Deuteronomy 2, Joshua 2). The phrase "the word of the LORD came", used of later prophets such as Elijah, is never used of Moses. Exodus 6:10 Exodus 4:19 1 Kings 17:2

The LORD told Moses to write a memorial against Amalek and the words of the covenant; Scripture says Moses wrote "all the words of the LORD", the stages of the journey, "this law", and a song taught to Israel. Exodus 17:14 Exodus 24:4 Exodus 34:27–28 Numbers 33:2 Deuteronomy 31:9 Deuteronomy 31:22 +1 more

He sang: the song at the sea, "Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD", and the song he spoke "in the ears of all the congregation" before his death. Revelation speaks of "the song of Moses the servant of God". Exodus 15:1 Deuteronomy 31:30 Deuteronomy 32:44 Revelation 15:3
KING OF EGYPT (NOT NAMED IN SCRIPTURE)
“Thus saith the LORD God of Israel, Let my people go, that they may hold a feast unto me in the wilderness.”
The word in its main themes
“I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.”
“Israel is my son, even my firstborn”
“Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.”
Blessing and curse set before them
“I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live”
A prophet like Moses, and how to know a true word
“The LORD thy God will raise up unto thee a Prophet from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken”
“When a prophet speaketh in the name of the LORD, if the thing follow not, nor come to pass, that is the thing which the LORD hath not spoken”
“would God that all the LORD’s people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!”
To whom the word was spoken
“Thus saith the LORD, About midnight will I go out into the midst of Egypt: And all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die”
“Hereby ye shall know that the LORD hath sent me to do all these works; for I have not done them of mine own mind.”
“Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?”
“Happy art thou, O Israel: who is like unto thee, O people saved by the LORD”
The rod, the hand and the water
Who stood with him, and against him
The LORD told Moses he would see the land but not enter it, because at Meribah "ye sanctified me not in the midst of the children of Israel". Numbers 20:12 Deuteronomy 32:48–52

"So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, according to the word of the LORD." He was 120, "his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated"; "he buried him in a valley" over against Beth-peor, "but no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day". Deuteronomy 34:5–8
Jude says the archangel Michael "disputed about the body of Moses" with the devil. Jude 1:9
At the transfiguration Moses and Elias appeared and talked with Jesus; Luke says they "spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem". Matthew 17:3 Luke 9:30–31

Origen speaks of "the work entitled The Ascension of Moses (a little treatise, of which the Apostle Jude makes mention in his Epistle)", in which the archangel Michael disputes "with the devil regarding the body of Moses". The book is not part of Scripture.[27] Who says so: Origen, De Principiis 3.2.1, first half of the 3rd century
"The prevailing opinion in the early Church", revived by Kurtz, Auberlen and Tholuck, as reported by Keil (1871)

Keil reports this as the early church’s main reading, which applied the promise directly and only to Christ, comparing Numbers 12:6–8, Deuteronomy 34:10 and Hebrews 3. Keil himself calls that use of those verses "unwarrantable".[11]
von Hofmann, Baur and Knobel, as reported by Keil (1871)
Keil reports that these scholars restrict the promise to the prophets of the Old Testament, "to the exclusion of the Messiah". He rejects the limit.[11]
A line of prophets, with Christ included

Both read "a prophet" as the prophets God would send whenever Israel needed a mediator, so that Israel need not turn to soothsayers. Keil adds that Christ, "in whom the prophetic character culminated", is included. Driver says the passage refers to "a prophetical order", and "may be reasonably understood as including" an ideal prophet in whom the line would culminate.[11][23]

Scripture names particular things Moses wrote (see "How the word came"), but the verses themselves do not say who wrote the five books as a whole.
Deuteronomy 34:6 says only "he buried him", and that "no man knoweth of his sepulchre unto this day".
John’s Gospel reports people asking about "that prophet" (John 1:21, 1:25; 6:14; 7:40), but does not cite Deuteronomy 18 at those places.
Exodus does not name the Pharaoh Moses faced, and Scripture gives no year BC for his call.
